| [ASM-001](#ASM-001) | A resubmitted request starts again at Project Manager confirmation. | OPEN | The URS says requests can be resubmitted after denial or rejection but not where they re-enter the workflow. |
| [ASM-002](#ASM-002) | One responsive web application serves all roles through role-specific screens; there is no separate native mobile or back-office application. | OPEN | The URS asks for a web-based, mobile-responsive system with role-specific screens. |
| [ASM-003](#ASM-003) | Admin and HR are treated as one actor, Admin/HR. | CONFIRMED | URS §4.6 defines a single 'Admin/HR' role. Confirmed by the BA at the GATE-02 review, 2026-09-30. |
| <a id="ASM-004"></a>ASM-004 | Requirement priorities were proposed during analysis; the URS states none. | OPEN | The requirements catalog needs a priority for each item. |
| [ASM-005](#ASM-005) | The leave request status names (PENDING_CONFIRMATION, PENDING_APPROVAL, DENIED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) are proposed labels. | OPEN | The URS names the actions (confirm, deny, approve, reject) and gives 'pending, approved, denied' only as examples. |
| [ASM-006](#ASM-006) | Sign-in and sign-out are handled by the company's single sign-on, so this system has no sign-in use case of its own. | OPEN | Users sign in with the company's single sign-on (Q-005). |
| [ASM-007](#ASM-007) | A request can be reviewed at any time from submission up to the end of the month of the leave start date. | OPEN | The BA said a request for a later month can be reviewed at the end of that month and need not be reviewed before it starts; whether earlier review is allowed was not said. |
| [ASM-008](#ASM-008) | The managers who see leave reports are Line Managers. Project Managers have no access to reports. | OPEN | The BA said a manager sees reports for their own unit only, and only Line Managers manage a unit. |
| [ASM-009](#ASM-009) | 'The last week' in the weekly notification is the week that ends on the Friday the notification is sent. | OPEN | The BA said the period is the last week without naming its first and last day. |
| [ASM-010](#ASM-010) | The base days and N (years of service per extra day) are configured per leave type by Admin/HR. | OPEN | The system calculates entitlements as base days plus one day per N years of service and nothing is imported; URS §4.5 lets Admins configure the rules of each leave type. |
| [ASM-011](#ASM-011) | UC-006 keeps its ID but changes from an import by Admin/HR to an automatic annual refresh run by the system. | OPEN | The BA decided that no entitlement amounts are imported and that the refresh starts automatically at the start of the year. |
| [ASM-012](#ASM-012) | When a request skips confirmation (a Project Manager's own request, or an employee with no project), the Line Manager receives the email that confirmation would send. | OPEN | The BA defined the email for confirmation but not for requests that reach the Line Manager without one. |
| [ASM-013](#ASM-013) | Weekends are Saturday and Sunday in every country. | OPEN | The BA said weekends are not working days and that public holidays come from the HR system, but not which days are the weekend in each country. |
| [ASM-014](#ASM-014) | The company single sign-on supports OpenID Connect. | OPEN | The technical baseline signs users in with OpenID Connect; the protocol of the company identity provider was not given. |
| [ASM-015](#ASM-015) | The system runs as containers on a Kubernetes platform chosen by the client, with managed PostgreSQL and S3-compatible object storage available. | OPEN | The URS names no hosting environment; the BA delegated the technology choices. |
